judgment.grounding: Workspace sources establish that all 57 permit_limits.csv rows with empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR share LIMIT_TYPE_CODE=ENF but do not share a single obligation type. DMR_COMMENT_TEXT partitions 39 of 57 rows into geometric-mean TDS (15), WHEN DISCHARGING (12), and pass/fail WET (12); 18 rows have blank DMR_COMMENT_TEXT. Permit narratives in documents/gcc/final_permit.txt, documents/aztec/final_permit.txt, and documents/farmington/final_permit.txt corroborate report-only limitations, pass/fail 0/1 WET coding, geometric-mean reporting, and when-discharging conditions for matching parameters. LIMIT_VALUE_TYPE_CODE values (C1/C2/C3/Q1/Q2) appear on both empty and nonempty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR rows and do not discriminate. No FY2025 DMR measurement rows in this workspace have empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR, so Purpose A comparison behavior for these rows is unobservable.
judgment.interpretation: Empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR does not uniformly denote an enforceable numeric concentration limit or uniform report-only monitoring. It marks multiple distinct non-numeric or non-concentration obligation types—report-only monitoring, pass/fail coded WET reporting, geometric-mean aggregated reporting, and conditional when-discharging monitoring—rather than a single recoverable numeric limit value.
judgment.remaining_uncertainty: Eighteen of 57 empty-limit rows have blank DMR_COMMENT_TEXT with no structured classifier; their obligation type is not established from structured fields alone. No workspace codebook defines LIMIT_VALUE_TYPE_CODE or empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR semantics. Whether discharge occurred for when-discharging rows is not established in structured sources. Geometric-mean TDS rows may relate to separate numeric limits elsewhere in permit schedules. Purpose A numeric comparison for empty-limit rows cannot be observed from FY2025 DMR data in this workspace.

Exclude all such rows from numeric_comparison_candidate; do not treat absence of LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR as numeric non-compliance.

children.exact_semantic_question: When LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR is empty and DMR_COMMENT_TEXT is blank, is the row report-only monitoring with no numeric concentration limit for comparison?
When LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR is empty and DMR_COMMENT_TEXT references geometric mean reporting, is the row an aggregated reporting obligation rather than a per-period numeric concentration limit?
When LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR is empty and DMR_COMMENT_TEXT is 'WHEN DISCHARGING.', is the row conditional monitoring/reporting (not a standing numeric limit) whose applicability depends on discharge?
When LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR is empty and DMR_COMMENT_TEXT specifies PASS=0/FAIL=1 reporting, is the row a pass/fail coded WET obligation rather than a numeric concentration limit?

refinement.why_necessary: Retrieved permit text and DMR_COMMENT_TEXT show that empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR does not denote one homogeneous class. The 57 affected rows partition into four materially different obligation types: plain report-only monitoring (permit 'Report' limits), geometric-mean TDS reporting, conditional when-discharging monitoring, and pass/fail coded WET (0/1 vs critical dilution). A single parent answer of 'numeric limit', 'report-only', or 'something else' would misclassify a large fraction of rows.

occurrence_partition.rule: Partition permit_limits.csv rows with empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR by DMR_COMMENT_TEXT pattern, in priority order: (1) contains 'PASS = 0' and 'FAIL = 1' -> pass_fail_coded_wet; (2) contains 'GEOMETRIC MEAN' -> geometric_mean_reporting; (3) equals or starts with 'WHEN DISCHARGING' -> conditional_when_discharging; (4) otherwise -> report_only_monitoring.

mechanically_computable.notes: DMR_COMMENT_TEXT alone mechanically partitions all 57 rows. Resolving the report-only subclass (blank comment) still requires permit narrative crosswalk; the other three subclasses are established by DMR comment plus matching permit excerpts already retrieved.
